title: 273. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Exponential Function Growth and Decay Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Identifying Exponential Decay from the Base
questions.learningObjective: Identify which exponential function represents decay by examining the base.
questions.question: Which function represents exponential decay?
questions.explanation: An exponential function \(y=b^x\) represents decay when \(0<b<1\). For \(y=3^x\), the base is \(3>1\), so the function represents growth. For \(y=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x\), the base is \(\frac{1}{3}\), which satisfies \(0<\frac{1}{3}<1\), so the function represents decay. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether the base is between \(0\) and \(1\) or greater than \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the \(y\)-intercept of a basic exponential function.
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=2^x\)?
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept occurs when \(x=0\). Substitute \(x=0\) into \(y=2^x\): \(y=2^0=1\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,1)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Substitute \(x=0\) and use the fact that \(b^0=1\) for any \(b>0\).

questions.concept: Horizontal Asymptote of a Basic Exponential Function
questions.learningObjective: Identify the horizontal asymptote of a basic exponential function.
questions.question: What is the horizontal asymptote of the graph of \(y=2^x\)?
questions.explanation: As \(x\to-\infty\), \(2^x\) approaches \(0\) but never equals \(0\). Therefore the horizontal asymptote is \(y=0\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Consider the behavior of \(b^x\) as \(x\) becomes very negative.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a basic exponential function.
questions.question: What is the domain of \(y=3^x\)?
questions.explanation: The expression \(3^x\) is defined for every real number \(x\), including negative values, zero, and positive values. Therefore the domain is all real numbers, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Consider whether negative and non-integer exponents are allowed.

questions.concept: Range of a Basic Exponential Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a basic exponential function.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=2^x\)?
questions.explanation: For any real number \(x\), \(2^x\) is always positive. The value \(0\) is never attained; instead, \(2^x\) approaches \(0\) as \(x\to-\infty\) and grows without bound as \(x\to\infty\). Therefore the range is \(y>0\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall that \(b^x\) is always positive when \(b>0\).

questions.concept: Identifying Exponential Decay from the Base
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an exponential function represents growth or decay.
questions.question: Does the function \(y=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^x\) represent exponential growth or decay?
questions.explanation: An exponential function \(y=b^x\) represents decay when \(0<b<1\). Here the base is \(\frac{1}{4}\), which lies between \(0\) and \(1\). Therefore the function represents decay, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the base with the number \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine which exponential function has an increasing graph.
questions.question: Which function has an increasing graph?
questions.explanation: An exponential function \(y=b^x\) is increasing when \(b>1\) and decreasing when \(0<b<1\). For \(y=5^x\), the base is \(5>1\), so the graph increases. For \(y=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^x\), the base is \(\frac{1}{5}\), so the graph decreases. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: A base greater than \(1\) produces an increasing graph.

questions.concept: Horizontal Asymptote of a Shifted Exponential Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the horizontal asymptote of a vertically shifted exponential function.
questions.question: What is the horizontal asymptote of \(y=2^x+3\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y=2^x+3\) is the graph of \(y=2^x\) shifted upward by \(3\) units. The horizontal asymptote of \(y=2^x\) is \(y=0\), so after shifting upward by \(3\) units, the new horizontal asymptote is \(y=3\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: A vertical shift moves the horizontal asymptote by the same amount.

questions.concept: Range of a Shifted Exponential Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of an exponential function after a vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=2^x-4\)?
questions.explanation: The expression \(2^x\) is always positive and approaches \(0\) as \(x\to-\infty\). Therefore \(2^x-4\) is always greater than \(-4\) and approaches \(-4\) but never equals it. Hence the range is \(y>-4\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Determine whether the value at the asymptote is included in the range.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the growth rates of two exponential functions with different bases.
questions.question: For \(x>0\), which function grows faster?
questions.explanation: For \(x>0\), both functions are increasing, but the one with the larger base grows faster. Since \(3>2\), we have \(3^x>2^x\) for every \(x>0\). For example, at \(x=2\), \(3^2=9\) while \(2^2=4\). Therefore \(y=3^x\) grows faster, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the bases of the two exponential functions.
